phase_meta.name: Crushing & Processing
phase_meta.transformation: Raw bean to soy cake and oil

synthetic.name: Land Conversion & Farm
synthetic.notes: Frontier expansion driven by weak land governance. 149,649 ha deforested in Argentina in 2024. Land title disputes and zoning manipulation documented.
synthetic.data_quality: Low — farm-level deforestation data not publicly disclosed per plot

synthetic.name: Cultivation & Harvest
synthetic.notes: Primary production well-documented at national level. Farm-level provenance remains opaque. Certified volumes (RTRS) under 1%.
synthetic.data_quality: Medium — national aggregates reliable; farm-level provenance opaque

synthetic.name: Aggregation & Transport
synthetic.notes: BOTTLENECK. Beans from multiple origins commingled at silos. Sio-granos data aggregated by zone, not farm. 82% of imports from Paraguay — mixed without origin segregation.
synthetic.data_quality: Low — Sio-granos publicly available only in aggregated form; origin mixing is the core traceability gap

synthetic.name: Crushing & Processing
synthetic.notes: World-class crushing hub at Rosario. 62 Mt/year capacity, 60% utilisation. Operations well-documented by CIARA and Bolsa de Cereales.
synthetic.data_quality: High — crusher operations and trade volumes tracked by industry associations

synthetic.name: Export & EUDR Compliance
synthetic.notes: Export data well-documented. EUDR creates compliance pressure but Chaco is currently excluded from EUDR scope (canopy threshold gap). 55% ZDC coverage as of 2019.
synthetic.data_quality: Medium — volumes reliable; EUDR compliance status unresolved for Chaco-origin soy

system.interpretation: The Gran Chaco soy supply chain scores A+ (81.2% average balance). Phase 2 — Aggregation and Transport — is the structural bottleneck at 62.9% (Poor). The commingling of soybeans from multiple geographic origins at silo collection points severs the provenance chain required for EUDR compliance, deforestation-free certification, and sustainability-linked bond KPI verification. The D-C imbalance at Phase 2 (D=220, C=350) reflects a system that integrates volumes efficiently but cannot govern their origin. Resolving this bottleneck — via disaggregated Sio-granos disclosure, isotopic fingerprinting, or trader-level data sharing — would raise the chain grade to AA- or better.
